definition: A set of harmful behaviour requests used as the target list for jailbreak attacks and, correspondingly, as one of the safety benchmarks a defence is scored on. Both sources here use it as one of several, and its role in this archive is as the easiest of them: the dual-adversarial defence work reports attack success falling from 65.77 to 1.92 on it -- to 0.00 on three of eight models -- while the same defences leave 9.00 to 44.75 on the harder HarmBench, so a near-zero score here is not evidence of a solved problem. The attack source uses it alongside StrongREJECT to show automated hijacking of safety reasoning. Neither describes its construction.

evidence.note: Builds safety-alignment training data by first having an agent jailbreak a strong teacher and only then asking that teacher to explain why the successful attack worked, so the student is supervised on the mechanism of the attack rather than on the refusal.
evidence.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

evidence.note: Automates the hijacking of a reasoning model's own safety reasoning by using a weaker, less-aligned model to simulate execution reasoning and refining attacks from patterns leaked in refusals.
evidence.title: AutoRAN: Automated Hijacking of Safety Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models

name: AdvBench
